headline: AGNICO EAGLE MAPS 20%-30% GOLD PRODUCTION GROWTH AT D&D — Detour Lake On Path To 1Moz/Yr, Organic-First
snippet: Agnico Eagle (TSX/NYSE: AEM) used the Diggers & Dealers Mining Forum on August 3, 2026 to detail a multi-year organic growth plan targeting 20%–30% production growth from its current ~3.4 million oz/year run rate over 5–10 years, with a stated 'clear pathway' for Detour Lake alone to reach 1 million oz/year sustained for decades — supported by adding ~25 million oz of resources at both Detour Lake and Canadian Malartic through exploration over the past decade. Management reaffirmed a rule-of-law jurisdiction focus and preference for organic expansion over large acquisitions, making its exploration portfolio directly relevant to junior miners with district-scale ground in Quebec and Ontario, and its production targets a key benchmark for the gold sector's re-rating thesis.

headline: EVOLUTION MINING MEETS FY26 GUIDANCE WITH RECORD $1.39B CASH FLOW — Fully Unhedged; Net Cash $1.35B (ASX: EVN)
snippet: Evolution Mining (ASX: EVN) confirmed it met FY26 gold production and cost guidance at Diggers & Dealers on August 3, 2026, producing 715,000 oz at AISC of A$1,717/oz while generating record Group cash flow of A$1,389 million at a margin of A$1,958/oz. The balance sheet transformation stands out: Evolution is now fully unhedged and carries net cash of A$1,347 million, with all high-return organic growth projects at Northparkes, Cowal, and Ernest Henry remaining on schedule and budget. Formal FY27 guidance is due August 19 — a potentially significant market catalyst given gold's 30%+ year-to-date move and the operating leverage embedded in an unhedged, net-cash balance sheet.

headline: COPPER SURGES TO $6.47/LB — Two-Week High On China Supply Tightness And Fed Hold; Up 45.8% Year-On-Year
snippet: LME copper climbed to US$6.47/lb on August 3, 2026 — up 0.55% on the day and the highest in two weeks — driven by shortages of copper concentrate and scrap in China pushing treatment charges higher, with support from the Federal Reserve's July 30 decision to hold rates at 5.50%. Year-over-year, copper is up 45.8%, and the AI data-centre buildout and clean energy transition continue to underpin analyst demand-side models. For junior copper developer valuations, Capstone's reported Q2 realized price of US$6.22/lb combined with today's spot provides a critical benchmark for resource-stage NPV calculations — and reinforces the case for the current cycle extending into 2027.

headline: FRANK HOLMES: GOLD BULL FAR FROM OVER — Asian Demand And Central Banks Are The Floor; Targets $5K Then $7K
snippet: Frank E. Holmes of U.S. Global Investors told Money Metals Exchange on August 1, 2026 that the gold bull market remains structurally intact despite the pullback from January's US$5,600 peak, arguing that Asian demand and ongoing central bank accumulation — not Western retail flows — are the price floor at current $4,000–4,100 levels. Holmes targets $5,000 as the near-term price point and $7,000 as his end-of-Trump-second-term call, citing fiscal dynamics that virtually guarantee continued dollar debasement pressure. For junior mining investors tracking sector sentiment, the Holmes framework — that the gold bull is early-innings at $4,000 — is a contrarian anchor at a moment when institutional rotation back into gold equities is still gaining momentum.

headline: GALLEON GOLD DRILLS 6.8 g/t Au OVER 19.45m AT WEST CACHE — Zone #9 Now Extends To 500m Vertical (TSX-V: GGO)
snippet: Galleon Gold Corp (TSX-V: GGO) reported July 30, 2026 that additional drilling at its 100%-owned West Cache Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario has confirmed the high-grade core of Zone #9 with hole WC-26-251 returning 6.8 g/t Au over 19.45 metres including 16.84 g/t Au over 6.15 metres, plus a second hole at 6.25 g/t Au over 10.2 metres. The Zone #9 corridor now extends to approximately 500 metres vertical depth with the system remaining open, converging toward the historic high-grade West Deep zone — a depth extension that substantially expands the mineable envelope at a project in the established Timmins gold camp with existing nearby infrastructure. For investors tracking Ontario gold explorers, Zone #9 grade continuity at depth is a key milestone toward advancing to resource definition.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER TRIPLES MINTO M&I TO 47.8Mt — 940Mlb Copper And 530Koz Gold In Yukon (TSX-V: SCMI)
source_name: The Deep Dive / Selkirk Copper Mines
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines (TSX-V: SCMI) announced on July 30, 2026 an updated 43-101 mineral resource estimate for its Minto copper-gold-silver project in the Yukon that nearly triples measured and indicated tonnage to 47.8 million tonnes at 0.89% Cu, 0.34 g/t Au, and 3.2 g/t Ag — containing 940 million pounds of copper, 530,000 ounces of gold, and 4.97 million ounces of silver, representing 182%, 184%, and 188% increases respectively over the 2025 estimate. The resource is split between an underground component (26Mt at 1.14% Cu, 0.49 g/t Au) and an open-pit component (21.8Mt at 0.59% Cu), offering development optionality in a brownfield camp that already has infrastructure from its prior producing mine phase — a key advantage when copper is trading above US$6.40/lb.

headline: T2 METALS DRILLS FIRST HOLES IN 15 YEARS AT AURORA — Yukon Dawson District Gold-Silver; 76 km² Target
source_name: Investing News Network / T2 Metals Corp.
snippet: T2 Metals Corp (TSX-V: TWO) commenced its maiden drill program at the Aurora Gold-Silver Project in the Yukon's Dawson Mining District on July 30, 2026 — the first drilling at Aurora in over 15 years and the first-ever systematic drill test of the project's multiple gold, silver, copper, and antimony targets across a 76 km² land package staked by renowned prospector Shawn Ryan in 2004. Aurora sits only 8 km west of Prospector Metals' ML Project, where recent drilling returned 44 metres averaging 13.79 g/t gold and 1.84% copper, giving the district a fresh discovery context. With fewer than 3,000 metres of historical drilling total, Aurora is essentially a greenfield target in a proven Yukon gold corridor — the type of first-drill catalyst that has historically driven significant re-ratings for TSX-V juniors.

headline: ALAMOS GOLD CUTS FULL-YEAR GUIDANCE 12% AFTER YOUNG-DAVIDSON SEISMIC — New Range 510-560Koz (TSX: AGI)
snippet: Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI, NYSE: AGI) reported Q2 2026 results on July 29 showing a 12% reduction to its full-year gold production guidance — from 580,000–640,000 oz to 510,000–560,000 oz — after a seismic event at the Young-Davidson mine in Ontario caused slower mining rates, while delayed recoveries at La Yaqui Grande in Mexico compounded the shortfall. Revenue still rose 36% year-over-year to US$594 million, driven by a gold price that averaged US$4,483/oz in Q2, and Island Gold achieved record quarterly production of 67,500 oz. The operational setback is a reminder of the rock mechanics and geological risk embedded in open-pit and underground transitions — and the extent to which a single event can swing a 600,000+ oz producer's annual guidance in a material way.

headline: ENERGY FUELS BREAKS GROUND ON $104M HEAVY RARE EARTH PLANT — First Commercial HRE Separator Outside China (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU, TSX: EFR) announced July 29, 2026 that construction has commenced on a commercial-scale heavy rare earth separation facility at the White Mesa Mill in Utah — the first such plant outside China capable of commercially separating terbium, dysprosium, samarium, europium, and gadolinium. The US$104 million project is expected to be operational in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by US government grants and existing company capital. A new mixed rare earth carbonate circuit will allow simultaneous uranium and heavy REE oxide production — a strategic dual-commodity capability that directly addresses the supply chain vulnerability exposed by China's 2025 MOFCOM export licensing enforcement and positions White Mesa as the Western world's only facility capable of processing both uranium and heavy REEs at commercial scale.

headline: ABITIBI METALS FINDS NEW VMS ZONE 1.5km WEST OF B26 — 14.25m At 51.51 g/t Ag And 1.13% Zn In Quebec
source_name: The Prospector News / Abitibi Metals Corp.
snippet: Abitibi Metals Corp. (TSX-V: AMQ) announced July 29, 2026 that its first systematic test of the regional potential surrounding the B26 copper-gold deposit in western Quebec has intersected a new potential volcanogenic massive sulphide zinc-silver zone 1.5 kilometres west of B26 — with drill hole 1274-26-383 returning 14.25 metres of 1.13% zinc and 51.51 g/t silver at 400 metres vertical depth, open in all directions. The metal zonation mirrors B26's architecture where zinc-silver sits adjacent to the main copper-gold horizon, supporting the interpretation that this Target 1 hosts a distinct but analogous VMS system. With Discovery Silver holding a 9.9% stake in Abitibi, this regional discovery — suggesting B26 is part of a broader VMS cluster rather than a standalone deposit — meaningfully expands the district's total endowment potential.
